reply.result:
**Question:** If an input file or stream contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8 text — a common occurrence in real log files — should the tool pass those bytes through untouched and continue, or treat the input as unreadable and fail? (FR-005, FR-028)

**Why it matters:** The spec currently assumes any undecodable byte makes the whole file "unreadable" (exit status 2). Because such a byte can sit anywhere in a large file, that rule means a single stray byte near the end of a 1 GB log aborts the run after most of the redacted output has already been written — the operator gets a loud failure but no usable result.

**Recommended:** Option A — It keeps the tool's central promise ("everything else is output unchanged") true at the byte level, and it is not a silent-wrong-answer risk: undecodable bytes cannot look like an email, an address, or a digit run, and any text around them is still matched normally. A digit run interrupted by a stray byte is genuinely not a contiguous card number under FR-016, so nothing that should be redacted gets missed. Choosing this replaces the current assumption in the spec.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Pass undecodable bytes through unchanged and keep processing. Redaction applies normally to the surrounding text; the run still exits 0. |
| B | Keep the spec's current rule: any undecodable byte makes that source unreadable — name the file on standard error, stop reading further sources, exit 2 (output already written stays written). |
| C | Substitute a replacement character for each undecodable byte and continue, exiting 0. |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (≤5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
